## Intent
Hypothesis: scalar element-wise AoS processing with branchy respawn can achieve acceptable performance because cache residency compensates for per-particle instruction overhead.

## Layout & approach
The 68 B/particle AoS layout offers 32 hot bytes for loop 1 (47% of each line) and 28 for loop 2 (41%) — over half is dead weight. No intermediate storage keeps the death verdict in registers, fusing integration and respawn but forcing per-particle control-flow divergence. The approach is scalar: FP ops, conditional branches, and byte-level load-modify-stores per particle. The working set spills L1d at N≈481 and L2 at N≈7710, but high instruction count should keep it compute-bound regardless of cache level.

## Cache saturation
Cost is strikingly flat: ~22 ns/p in L1d (N=320–480), rising to ~25 ns/p through L2 (N=720–7700), holding ~24–25 ns/p through L3 and DRAM (N=10000–10000000). No sharp knee at any spill — L1d→L2 adds ~14%; L2→L3 and L3→DRAM are invisible. At q=0.01, cost spans only 22.1–25.5 ns/p across five orders of magnitude in N. The algo is too compute/branch-bound for cache capacity to matter, refuting the residency-compensation hypothesis.

## Bandwidth
Achieved 2.66–3.10 GB/s — 21–24% of the 12.69 GB/s ceiling, 4–6x above the 5.359 ns/p floor (22–34 ns/p). Compute/branch-bound. The 1.0x baseline ratio everywhere confirms this IS the baseline. vs the winner: 2.986x slower at q=0.01/N=320, peaking at 3.585x at N=160000, narrowing to 2.433x at N=10000000 as the winner also hits DRAM. Death rate drives cost linearly: q=0.01→~25 ns/p, q=0.5→~33.5 ns/p (+34%), as branch_flush rises 11.3%→14.7%. The gap narrows from ~3x to ~2x — branchy respawn is the equalizer.

## Assembly
Entirely scalar: vmovss/vmulss/vaddss for all FP, only 4 vector-suffixed instructions in 360. Loop 1 runs ~118 insns/iter with 14 conditional branches on stride-68B; branchy respawn (jae → call spawn → Random.fill → lzcnt) blocks vectorization. Byte-granular scatter (×12 loop 1, ×16 loop 2) uses movzx+add+cmp+cmovae+mov BYTE PTR — each color channel a byte load-modify-store, explaining the 60–67% backend_stall. vucomiss+jae death checks drive branch_flush (11–15%). Loop 2's cmovae selects (×12) reduce branching but byte scatter dominates.

## Verdict
Refuted — 1.0x of baseline everywhere (it IS the baseline) and 2.4–3.6x slower than the winner at q=0.01, narrowing to 1.8–2.0x at q=0.5. The residency-compensation hypothesis fails: cost is flat at 22–25.5 ns/p across all cache regimes. Scalar FP, 14–21 branches per iteration, and byte-granular scatter cap bandwidth at 21–24% of ceiling with backend_stall at 60–67%. At q=0.5 the gap narrows to ~1.8x as branch_flush rises to 14.7% and the winner's respawn also degrades.
